stats.title: Page heading of the Stats page. Keep short, about 8 characters.
stats.subtitle: Subtitle under the Stats page heading. The Deadlock API is a service name and stays untranslated.
stats.refresh: Button on the Stats and Match history pages that reloads the match history. Keep short, about 10 characters.
stats.hero_fallback: Fallback hero label when a hero's name is unknown. {id} = numeric hero ID, e.g. 15. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
stats.unknown_hero: Fallback label for a hero that could not be identified, shown in a match row. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
stats.api_error: Error message when the Deadlock API answered with an error. {status} = HTTP status code, e.g. 500. The Deadlock API is a service name.
stats.cached_note: Note shown when the Deadlock API could not be reached and an older saved copy is shown. {time} = date and time of the saved copy, e.g. "Oct 28, 6:30 PM".

gate.no_account: Empty state on Stats and Match history pages when no Steam account is found. Steam is the game platform.
gate.error: Error state on Stats and Match history pages when the history could not be loaded. {error} = reason text, e.g. "The Deadlock API returned an error (500)."
gate.loading: Screen reader only text on the loading skeleton of the match history. Not visible. Keep the three dots.

scope.ranked: Label for ranked matches, used as a match mode badge in match rows and as a filter option. Ranked is a Deadlock game mode, match the game. Keep short, about 8 characters.
scope.unranked: Label for unranked matches, used as a match mode badge in match rows and as a filter option. Match the game's own wording. Keep short, about 10 characters.
scope.all: Filter option in the match history mode dropdown that shows every game mode. Keep short, about 10 characters.

stats.syncing: Small badge with a hover hint. {count} = number of matches still syncing, e.g. 3. Plural forms. One form has no number. Keep short, about 10 characters.
stats.syncing_hint: Tooltip on the syncing badge. Explains the match was read from the game and is not yet in the Deadlock API. Plural forms, one or several matches.

outcome.win: Stamp text on the match front page photo for a won match. Keep short, about 5 characters.
outcome.loss: Stamp text on the match front page photo for a lost match. Keep short, about 5 characters.

stats.record: Win and loss record in the match history summary strip. {wins} = wins, e.g. 12. {losses} = losses, e.g. 8. W and L are short for win and loss. Keep short, about 8 characters.
stats.record_unscored: Win and loss record in the summary strip with matches not scored. {wins} = wins, e.g. 12. {losses} = losses, e.g. 8. {unscored} = matches without a result, e.g. 2.
stats.playtime_hm: Play time on the Stats page. {hours} = whole hours, e.g. 25. {minutes} = minutes, e.g. 40. h and m are unit letters. Keep short, about 8 characters.
stats.playtime_m: Play time under one hour. {minutes} = minutes, e.g. 40. m is the unit letter. Keep short, about 4 characters.

filter.days: Option in the match history time range dropdown. {count} = number of days, e.g. 30. Plural forms. Keep short, about 8 characters.
filter.all_time: Option in the match history time range dropdown that removes the time limit. Keep short, about 8 characters.

summary.winrate: Small label above a number in the summary strip. Percentage of games won. Keep short, about 8 characters.
summary.form_aria: Screen reader label of the row of recent win and loss dots. {count} = number of games shown, e.g. 10.
summary.streak: Label of a stat tile on the Stats page for the current win or loss streak. Keep short, about 8 characters.
summary.streak_wins: Value of the streak tile. {count} = wins in a row, e.g. 4. Plural forms. Keep short, about 8 characters.
summary.streak_losses: Value of the streak tile. {count} = losses in a row, e.g. 3. Plural forms. Keep short, about 9 characters.
summary.streak_best: Small text under the streak tile. {wins} = longest win streak, e.g. 7. {losses} = longest loss streak, e.g. 4.
summary.playtime: Label of a stat tile on the Stats page for total time played. Keep short, about 10 characters.
summary.matches: Small text under the playtime tile. {count} = number of matches, e.g. 42.

highlights.most_played: Label above the user's most played hero in the summary strip and highlights. Hero is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 12 characters.
highlights.most_played_summary: Text under the most played hero. {games} = number of games, e.g. 38. {winrate} = percent, e.g. "54%".
highlights.best: Label above the hero with the best winrate. {min} = minimum games needed, e.g. 5. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
highlights.best_summary: Text under the best winrate hero. {winrate} = percent, e.g. "62%". {games} = number of games, e.g. 14.
highlights.best_empty: Empty hint where the best winrate hero would show. {min} = minimum games needed, e.g. 5. Hero is a Deadlock game term.

heroes.heading: Section heading on the Stats page above the list of per hero stats. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
heroes.intro: Intro text under the Heroes heading. {days} = number of days, e.g. 30. {games} = number of games, e.g. 50. Hero leaderboard is a Deadlock game term, match the game.
heroes.eligible: Small status line on a hero card. The user qualifies for that hero's leaderboard. Hero leaderboard is a Deadlock game term, match the game.
heroes.not_yet: Small status line on a hero card. The user does not yet qualify for that hero's leaderboard. Hero leaderboard is a Deadlock game term, match the game.
heroes.games: Small label above a number on a hero card for number of games played. Keep short, about 8 characters.
heroes.kda: Small label on a hero card and in the summary strip for the kills, deaths, assists ratio. Abbreviation, may stay KDA. Keep short, about 5 characters.
heroes.avg_souls: Small label for average souls per game, on a hero card and in the summary strip. Souls is a Deadlock game term, match the game. Keep short, about 12 characters.
heroes.time: Small label above a number on a hero card for time played. Keep short, about 6 characters.
heroes.none: Empty state on a hero card when the hero has no games in the current filters.
heroes.none_lifetime: Empty state on a hero card with no games in the current filters. {games} = lifetime games on that hero, e.g. 120.
heroes.recent_games: Label of a progress bar on a hero card. {days} = number of days, e.g. 30. Counts games in that window.
heroes.lifetime_wins: Label of a progress bar on a hero card for total wins ever on that hero.
heroes.builds: Link on a hero card that opens the Builds page for that hero. Hero is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 8 characters.
heroes.builds_label: Screen reader label of the builds link on a hero card. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.

region.heading: Card heading on the Stats page for the regional leaderboard.
region.eligible: Status text in the region leaderboard card heading. The user qualifies. Keep short, about 10 characters.
region.not_eligible: Status text in the region leaderboard card heading. The user does not qualify yet. Keep short, about 18 characters.
region.note: Note under the region leaderboard heading. The Deadlock API is a service name. Valve is a company name and stays untranslated.
region.recent_games: Label of a progress bar in the region leaderboard card. {days} = number of days, e.g. 30.
region.total_games: Label of a progress bar in the region leaderboard card for all games ever played on the account.
region.rank_error: Error message. Shown on the Stats page in place of the rank section when the user's rank could not be loaded.
region.games_error: Error message. Shown on the Stats page in place of the match list when the user's match history could not be loaded.

page.matches_known: Note on the Stats page. {count} = number of matches known, e.g. 120. The count may be 1 or more.
page.empty: Empty state on the Stats page when no match fits the current filters.

section.games: Section heading on the Stats page above the match list. Keep short, about 12 characters.

stats.captured_only: Notice shown on the Stats page when the Deadlock API (the data service) is unreachable. Only matches the app recorded on this PC are listed.

rank.title: Section heading on the Stats page for the user's competitive rank. Match the game's own wording. Keep short, about 8 characters.
rank.empty: Empty state in the rank section when no rank data exists. The Deadlock API is a service name. Placement games are the first ranked games.
rank.tier_fallback: Fallback rank name when the tier name is unknown. {tier} = tier number, e.g. 7. Ranks are Deadlock game terms.

eta.not_climbing: Estimate text for when the user would reach the next rank. Used when the recent pace is not rising.
eta.days_or_more: Estimate text for reaching the next rank. {low} = minimum days, e.g. 14.
eta.about: Estimate text for reaching the next rank in about this many days. {count} = days, e.g. 10. Plural forms. Starts with a capital.
eta.range: Estimate text for reaching the next rank. {low} = fewest days, e.g. 10. {high} = most days, e.g. 20.

form.next_win: Label of a stat tile in the rank section for the rank points gained by the next win. Keep short, about 10 characters.
form.no_streak: Small text under the next win tile when the user has no current win streak.
form.streak: Small text under the next win tile. {count} = current win streak, e.g. 3. Plural forms.
form.next_loss: Label of a stat tile in the rank section for the rank points lost by the next loss. Keep short, about 10 characters.
form.only_shield: Small text under the next loss tile. The next loss only uses up a demotion shield, no points lost. Shield is a Deadlock rank term, match the game.
form.plus_shield: Small text under the next loss tile. The next loss costs points and also uses a demotion shield. Shield is a Deadlock rank term, match the game.
form.drops_subrank: Small text under the next loss tile. The user has no shield, so a loss would drop one subrank. Shield is a Deadlock rank term.
form.no_shield_used: Small text under the next loss tile. A loss would not use a demotion shield. Shield is a Deadlock rank term.

outlook.hold_rank: Small label above a percentage in the Outlook card. The winrate needed to keep the current rank.
outlook.no_data: Small explanation in the Outlook card. Shows when there is no recent form data. Winning streaks give more rank points than losses take.
outlook.climbing: Sentence in the Outlook card. {winrate} = percent, e.g. "58%". {count} = number of recent games, e.g. 10. Says the user is gaining rank.
outlook.sliding: Sentence in the Outlook card. {winrate} = percent, e.g. "42%". {count} = number of recent games, e.g. 10. Says the user is losing rank.
outlook.forecast_none: Small text in the Outlook card when there are too few recent ranked games to forecast the next rank.
outlook.hold: Sentence in the Outlook card. {winrate} = percent, e.g. "45%". The winrate that holds the current rank.
outlook.heading: Card heading in the rank section for the forecast of rank progress. Keep short, about 10 characters.
outlook.your_last: Small label in the Outlook card. {count} = number of recent games, e.g. 10. A percentage follows it.
outlook.climbing_short: Short status word in the Outlook card, green. The user is gaining rank. Keep short, about 10 characters.
outlook.sliding_short: Short status word in the Outlook card, red. The user is losing rank. Keep short, about 10 characters.
outlook.next_tier: Small text in the Outlook card. {eta} = estimate phrase, e.g. "About 10 days" or "10 to 20 days".

chart.heading: Card heading of the rank progress chart. Keep short, about 10 characters.
chart.last_n: Toggle button above the rank chart choosing how many recent matches to show. {count} = number of matches, e.g. 25. Keep short, about 9 characters.
chart.aria: Screen reader label of the rank progress chart.
chart.range: Small caption under the rank chart. {from} = starting rank name, e.g. "Ritualist 3". {to} = ending rank name. Ranks are Deadlock game terms.
chart.legend: Legend line under the rank chart explaining dot colours and rings. A shield is the demotion shield. Shield is a Deadlock rank term.
chart.empty: Empty state of the rank chart when there are too few ranked matches.
chart.legend_changes: Legend line under the rank chart explaining triangle markers on the line.

changes.promoted_from: Tooltip text on a chart marker. {name} = rank name before the promotion, e.g. "Ritualist 3". Ranks are Deadlock game terms.
changes.demoted_from: Tooltip text on a chart marker. {name} = rank name before the demotion, e.g. "Ritualist 3". Ranks are Deadlock game terms.

summary.estimated: Small note in the rank section. Rank is a guess from the rules, not yet confirmed by the Deadlock API (a service name). Plural forms, one or several matches.
summary.top_tier: Note in the rank section shown at the highest rank. Subranks here depend on comparison with other top players, so no progress bar.
summary.progress: Progress text under the rank bar. {within} = points gained in this rank, e.g. 12. {span} = points needed, e.g. 20. {next} = next rank name, e.g. "Ritualist 4".
summary.progress_aria: Screen reader label for the rank progress bar. {next} = name of the next rank, e.g. "Archon 3". Rank names are Deadlock game terms.
summary.progress_streak: Progress text under the rank bar with win streak info. {within} = points gained, e.g. 12. {span} = points needed, e.g. 20. {next} = next rank name. {count} = wins needed in a row, e.g. 3. Plural forms.
summary.boundary: Note in the rank section replacing the progress bar. The progress crossed a rank boundary but the Deadlock API (a service name) still shows the old badge.
summary.placement_left: Note in the rank section. {count} = placement games still to play, e.g. 4. Placement games are the first ranked games.

shields.heading: Label of a stat tile in the rank section for demotion shields, which protect from rank loss. Shield is a Deadlock rank term, match the game. Keep short, about 18 characters.
shields.not_reported: Small text in the shields tile when the shield count is not known. Keep short, about 14 characters.
shields.none_hint: Small text in the shields tile when the user has none. Losing can lower the rank.
shields.left_hint: Small text in the shields tile when the user has some. Each shield blocks one demotion.

sessions.title: Section heading on the Stats page above the play sessions analysis. A session is a block of matches played in a row.
sessions.subtitle: Tooltip on the info icon next to the Sessions heading. Explains how matches are grouped into sessions.

results.heading: Section heading on the Stats page above the insight cards about the user's results.
results.intro: Intro text under the results heading, explaining the winrate line on each bar chart. Winrate means share of games won.
results.intro_detail: Intro text under the results heading. {winrate} = overall winrate, e.g. "52%". {games} = number of games, e.g. 120.
results.hide: Button that collapses the results section on the Stats page. Keep short, about 6 characters.
results.show: Button that expands the results section on the Stats page. Keep short, about 6 characters.

break.label: Setting label next to a switch on the Sessions bar. Turns on a hint that suggests a break after losses.
break.suggestion: Status message on the Sessions bar after a losing streak. {count} = number of losses in a row, e.g. 3. Friendly, not pushy.

highlight.best: Title of a highlight card for the user's best recent play session.
highlight.excellent: Message in a highlight card after a very good last session. Friendly tone.
highlight.good: Message in a highlight card after a good last session. Friendly tone.

row.excellent: Label on a session header in Match History for a session with very good results. Keep short, about 18 characters.
row.good: Label on a session header in Match History for a good session. Keep short, about 14 characters.
row.bad: Label on a session header in Match History for a bad session. Keep short, about 14 characters.
row.neutral: Label on a session header in Match History for a session with average results. Keep short, about 14 characters.
row.games: Column label in a Match History session header, above the number of games played. Keep short, about 6 characters.
row.record: Column label in a Match History session header, above the wins and losses count. Keep short, about 7 characters.
row.length: Column label in a Match History session header, above how long the session lasted. Keep short, about 7 characters.
row.rank_change: Tooltip on the rank points change shown on a Match History row. Rank is a Deadlock game term.

findings.games: Game count under a bar in the session insight charts, plural forms. {count} = number of games, e.g. 12.

insights.unknown_after_loss: Insight text when there is too little data. {yes} and {no} = game counts, e.g. 4 and 7. {min} = minimum needed per group, e.g. 5.

after_losses.title: Title of an insight card about how the user plays after losses. Keep short, about 14 characters.
after_losses.unknown: Insight text when there is too little data. {games} = games counted so far, e.g. 2. {min} = games needed, e.g. 5.
after_losses.worse: Insight headline. {rate} = winrate after two losses, e.g. "40%". {rest} = winrate otherwise, e.g. "52%".
after_losses.better: Insight headline. {rate} = winrate after two losses, e.g. "58%". {rest} = winrate otherwise, e.g. "50%".
after_losses.same: Insight headline. {rate} = winrate after two losses, e.g. "51%". {rest} = winrate otherwise, e.g. "50%".
after_losses.bar_after: Bar label in an insight chart for games right after two losses in a row. Keep short, about 26 characters.
after_losses.bar_rest: Bar label in an insight chart for all other games. Keep short, about 16 characters.

session_length.title: Title of an insight card about how results change as a session gets longer. Keep short, about 14 characters.
session_length.bar: Bar label in an insight chart for one game in a session. {n} = game number in the session, e.g. 3. Keep short, about 8 characters.
session_length.bar_plus: Bar label in an insight chart for a game number and every later game. {n} = game number, e.g. 6. Keep short, about 9 characters.
session_length.points: Small note under a bar showing average rank points change. {amount} = signed number, e.g. "+12". Keep short, about 8 characters.
session_length.drop: Insight headline. {last} = game number, e.g. 4. {head} = winrate up to then, e.g. "55%". {tail} = winrate after, e.g. "42%". {from} = next game number, e.g. 5.
session_length.hold: Insight headline saying results stay steady in longer sessions.
session_length.unknown: Insight text when there is too little data. {games} = number of games past game 3, e.g. 2. {min} = games needed, e.g. 5. Game 3 is a fixed number in the text.

swap_hero.title: Title of an insight card about changing hero or staying after a loss. Keep short, about 16 characters.
swap_hero.bar_switched: Bar label in an insight chart for games where the user changed hero. Keep short, about 14 characters.
swap_hero.bar_same: Bar label in an insight chart for games with the same hero as before. Keep short, about 11 characters.
swap_hero.better: Insight headline. {yes} = winrate after switching heroes, e.g. "56%". {no} = winrate when staying on the same hero, e.g. "47%".
swap_hero.worse: Insight headline. {no} = winrate when staying on the same hero, e.g. "55%". {yes} = winrate when switching, e.g. "46%".
swap_hero.same: Insight headline. {yes} and {no} = winrates after switching and after staying, e.g. "50%" and "51%".

requeue.title: Title of an insight card about how fast the user queues again after a loss. Keep short, about 14 characters.
requeue.bar_quick: Bar label in an insight chart for games queued within 10 minutes of the last one. Keep short, about 24 characters.
requeue.bar_slow: Bar label in an insight chart for games queued after a longer wait. Keep short, about 14 characters.
requeue.better: Insight headline. {yes} = winrate when queueing straight back up, e.g. "56%". {no} = winrate when waiting longer, e.g. "47%".
requeue.worse: Insight headline. {no} = winrate when waiting longer, e.g. "55%". {yes} = winrate when queueing straight back up, e.g. "46%".
requeue.same: Insight headline. {yes} and {no} = winrates when queueing straight back and when waiting, e.g. "50%" and "51%".

time_of_day.title: Title of an insight card about results by time of day. Keep short, about 12 characters.
time_of_day.morning: Bar label in an insight chart for games played in the morning. Keep short, about 8 characters.
time_of_day.afternoon: Bar label in an insight chart for games played in the afternoon. Keep short, about 10 characters.
time_of_day.evening: Bar label in an insight chart for games played in the evening. Keep short, about 8 characters.
time_of_day.late_night: Bar label in an insight chart for games played late at night. Keep short, about 10 characters.
time_of_day.phrase_morning: Phrase inserted into a sentence as {best} or {worst}, e.g. "You do best in the morning". Must fit after the verb.
time_of_day.phrase_afternoon: Phrase inserted into a sentence as {best} or {worst}, e.g. "You do best in the afternoon". Must fit after the verb.
time_of_day.phrase_evening: Phrase inserted into a sentence as {best} or {worst}, e.g. "You do best in the evening". Must fit after the verb.
time_of_day.phrase_late_night: Phrase inserted into a sentence as {best} or {worst}, e.g. "You do best during the late night". Must fit after the verb.
time_of_day.best_worst: Insight headline. {best} and {worst} = time of day phrases. {best_rate} and {worst_rate} = winrates, e.g. "58%". {overall} = overall winrate, e.g. "51%".
time_of_day.best: Insight headline. {best} = time of day phrase, e.g. "in the evening". {best_rate} = winrate, e.g. "58%". {overall} = overall winrate, e.g. "51%".
time_of_day.worst: Insight headline. {worst} = time of day phrase, e.g. "in the morning". {worst_rate} = winrate, e.g. "44%". {overall} = overall winrate, e.g. "51%".
time_of_day.none: Insight headline when no time of day clearly stands out.
time_of_day.unknown: Insight text when there is too little data. {min} = games needed in each part of the day, e.g. 5.

day_type.title: Title of an insight card comparing weekdays and weekends. Keep short, about 22 characters.
day_type.weekdays: Bar label in an insight chart for games played Monday to Friday. Keep short, about 10 characters.
day_type.weekends: Bar label in an insight chart for games played on Saturday and Sunday. Keep short, about 10 characters.
day_type.unknown: Insight text when there is too little data. {weekday} and {weekend} = game counts so far, e.g. 3 and 8. {min} = games needed in each, e.g. 5.
day_type.better: Insight headline. {weekend_rate} and {weekday_rate} = winrates, e.g. "56%" and "49%".
day_type.worse: Insight headline. {weekday_rate} and {weekend_rate} = winrates, e.g. "56%" and "49%".
day_type.same: Insight headline. {weekday_rate} and {weekend_rate} = winrates, e.g. "50%" and "51%".

match_history.api_error: Error message when the Deadlock API fails. {status} = HTTP status code, e.g. 500. "Deadlock" stays untranslated.
match_history.detail_invalid: Error message on the match detail page when the Deadlock API sends data that cannot be used. "Deadlock" stays untranslated.

team.hidden_king: Name of one of the two teams in a match. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
team.archmother: Name of one of the two teams in a match. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.

list.title: Page heading of the Match History page.
list.subtitle: Subtitle under the Match History page heading. "Deadlock" stays untranslated.
list.empty: Empty state on the Match History page when the player has no matches yet. "Deadlock" stays untranslated.
list.no_results: Empty state on the Match History page when the filters hide every match.
list.count: Summary line counting matches in the list. Plural forms. {count} = number of matches, e.g. 3.
list.provisional: Small badge on a match row captured from the game but not yet confirmed. Keep short, about 11 characters.
list.provisional_hint: Tooltip on the Unconfirmed badge in a match row. "Deadlock" stays untranslated.

mode.custom: Match mode label in a match row, for custom matches. Keep short, about 6 characters.
mode.other: Match mode label in a match row, for modes that are not otherwise named. Keep short, about 5 characters.

outcome.unscored: Outcome label in a match row when the match has no win or loss. Keep short, about 10 characters.

filter.label: Screen reader label for the filter bar above the match list.
filter.mode: Label of the match mode filter (segmented control) above the match list. Keep short, about 4 characters.
filter.hero: Screen reader label of the hero filter dropdown above the match list. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
filter.outcome: Label of the win or loss filter (segmented control) above the match list. Keep short, about 7 characters.
filter.window: Label of the date range filter (segmented control) above the match list. Keep short, about 11 characters.
filter.any_hero: Dropdown option in the hero filter that removes the hero filter. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
filter.any_outcome: Option in the outcome filter that shows wins and losses. Keep short, about 12 characters.
filter.custom: Button above the match list that opens custom match settings. Keep short, about 14 characters.
filter.reset: Button above the match list that clears all filters. Keep short, about 13 characters.

pager.label: Screen reader label for the page navigation under the match list.

summary.label: Screen reader label for the totals block above the match list.
summary.matches: Label in the totals block above the match list, for the number of matches. Keep short, about 7 characters.

row.souls: Tooltip on the souls figure in a match row. Souls is a Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
row.duration: Tooltip on the match length in a match row.
row.kda_split: Tooltip on the kills / deaths / assists figure in a match row. Keep the slashes.
row.kda_ratio: Small text in a match row. {ratio} = kills plus assists per death, e.g. "3.2". KDA is the usual kills, deaths, assists abbreviation.

list.error: Error message. Shown on the Match History page when the match list could not be loaded.

deep_dive.not_available: Notice inside a match detail section when the data is missing for that match.
deep_dive.player_fallback: Name shown for a player whose name is unknown. {slot} = player number in the match, e.g. 4.

progress.heading: Section heading on the match detail page for charts of souls and damage over time. Souls is a Deadlock game term.
progress.souls: Toggle label that switches the progress charts to souls. Souls is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 5 characters.
progress.damage: Toggle label that switches the progress charts to damage. Keep short, about 6 characters.
progress.lead_heading: Small heading above the chart showing which team led over time.
progress.lead_aria: Screen reader label for the team lead chart.
progress.lead_hint: Caption under the team lead chart explaining the axis. Hidden King and Archmother are Deadlock game terms and should match the game's translation.
progress.lead_even: Chart tooltip text when neither team leads at that moment.
progress.others_range: Chart tooltip label for the value range of all players other than the selected one.
progress.player_heading: Small heading above the chart that follows the selected player.
progress.player_aria: Screen reader label for the chart showing the selected player against the rest.
progress.player_hint: Caption under the player chart explaining which line is the selected player.
progress.picker_aria: Screen reader label for the player picker in the souls and damage section. Souls is a Deadlock game term.

purchases.heading: Section heading on the match detail page for item and ability purchases over time.
purchases.slider_aria: Screen reader label for the slider that steps through purchases.
purchases.previous: Tooltip and screen reader label of a button that goes to the previous purchase action.
purchases.next: Tooltip and screen reader label of a button that goes to the next purchase action.
purchases.step: Position counter next to the purchase slider. {current} = current step, e.g. 3. {total} = number of steps, e.g. 40.
purchases.item_buy: Purchase list entry. {name} = item name. Item names are Deadlock game terms.
purchases.item_sell: Purchase list entry. {name} = item name. Item names are Deadlock game terms.
purchases.ability_unlock: Purchase list entry. {name} = ability name. Ability names are Deadlock game terms.
purchases.ability_upgrade: Purchase list entry. {name} = ability name. {count} = upgrade level reached, e.g. 2. {total} = max upgrades, e.g. 3. Ability is a Deadlock game term.
purchases.imbued: Small text on an item that was imbued on an ability. {ability} = ability name. Imbue and ability are Deadlock game terms.
purchases.holding: Small heading above the list of items the player held at the selected moment.
purchases.no_items: Empty state text when the player held no items at the selected moment.
purchases.abilities: Small heading above the list of abilities the player had unlocked at the selected moment. Ability is a Deadlock game term.
purchases.no_abilities: Empty state text when the player had no abilities unlocked yet. Ability is a Deadlock game term.
purchases.ability_level_aria: Screen reader label for the upgrade pips on an ability. {count} = upgrades taken, e.g. 2. {total} = max upgrades, e.g. 3.
purchases.list_aria: Screen reader label for the scrolling list of every purchase action.
purchases.picker_aria: Screen reader label for the player picker in the purchases section.

damage.heading: Section heading on the match detail page for the damage table between heroes. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
damage.hint: Help text and tooltip for the damage table. Rows are damage dealers, columns are targets. "Other damage" must match the column label.
damage.dealer: Corner header of the damage table for the rows, the player dealing damage. Keep short, about 6 characters.
damage.other: Table column header in the damage table, damage credited to the dealer themselves. Keep short, about 12 characters.
damage.target: Corner header of the damage table for the columns, the player taking damage. Keep short, about 6 characters.
damage.other_hint: Tooltip on the Other damage column header in the damage table.
damage.picker_aria: Screen reader label for the player picker in the damage section.

objectives.heading: Section heading on the match detail page for the objectives table. Objectives are Deadlock game terms.
objectives.objective: Table column header in the objectives table, the objective name. Keep short, about 9 characters.
objectives.owner: Table column header in the objectives table, the team that owned the objective. Keep short, about 5 characters.
objectives.destroyed: Table column header in the objectives table, the time it was destroyed. Keep short, about 9 characters.
objectives.players: Table column header in the objectives table, damage from players. Keep short, about 13 characters.
objectives.creeps: Table column header in the objectives table, damage from creeps (minions). Keep short, about 12 characters.
objectives.spirit: Table column header in the objectives table, spirit damage. Spirit is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 13 characters.
objectives.standing: Cell text in the objectives table for an objective that was still standing at the end of the match. Keep short, about 8 characters.
objectives.mid_boss: Row label in the objectives table for the neutral boss. Mid Boss is a Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
objectives.killed_by: Small text on the Mid Boss row. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Team names are Deadlock game terms.
objectives.claimed_by: Small text on the Mid Boss row. {team} = team name that picked up the reward, e.g. "The Archmother". Team names are Deadlock game terms.
objectives.kind_core: Name of an objective type in the objectives table. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
objectives.kind_guardian: Name of an objective type in the objectives table. Guardian is a Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
objectives.kind_walker: Name of an objective type in the objectives table. Walker is a Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
objectives.kind_patron: Name of an objective type in the objectives table. Patron is a Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
objectives.kind_shrine: Name of an objective type in the objectives table. Shrine is a Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
objectives.kind_base_guardian: Name of an objective type in the objectives table. Base Guardian is a Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
objectives.kind_unknown: Fallback name for an objective of unknown type in the objectives table.
objectives.indexed_name: Objective name with a number to tell copies apart. {name} = objective type, e.g. "Guardian". {index} = number, e.g. 2.

accolades.heading: Section heading on the match detail page for the accolades a player earned. Accolade is a Deadlock game term.
accolades.tier: Small pill next to an accolade. {tier} = tier number, e.g. 2. Keep short, about 6 characters.
accolades.hint: Help text under the accolades list. Accolade and tier are Deadlock game terms.
accolades.picker_aria: Screen reader label for the player picker in the accolades section.

names.item: Fallback name for an item the app cannot name. Item is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 4 characters.
names.ability: Fallback name for an ability the app cannot name. Ability is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 7 characters.
names.accolade: Fallback name for an accolade the app cannot name. Accolade is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 8 characters.

lanes.yellow: Lane colour name in a lane chip. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 6 characters.
lanes.blue: Lane colour name in a lane chip. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 4 characters.
lanes.green: Lane colour name in a lane chip. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 5 characters.
lanes.street_yellow: Street name for the yellow lane, shown with the lane colour. Proper name from the game's map, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 4 characters.
lanes.street_blue: Street name for the blue lane, shown with the lane colour. Proper name from the game's map, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 8 characters.
lanes.street_green: Street name for the green lane, shown with the lane colour. Proper name from the game's map, match the game's own translation. Keep short, about 9 characters.
lanes.named: Lane chip text. {colour} = lane colour name, e.g. "Yellow". {street} = street name, e.g. "York". Lane colours are Deadlock game terms.
lanes.ordinal: Lane chip text when the colour is unknown. {n} = lane number, e.g. 2. Keep short, about 6 characters.

detail.title: Page heading of the match detail page. {id} = match ID number, e.g. 12345678.
detail.back: Link at the top of the match detail page that goes back to the match list.
detail.loading: Loading message on the match detail page.
detail.error: Error message on the match detail page. {error} = reason text, e.g. "Network error".
detail.invalid: Error message on the match detail page when the match ID in the address is not valid.
detail.summary: Screen reader label for the summary block at the top of the match detail page.
detail.bans: Small label in the match summary before the list of banned heroes. Hero is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 4 characters.
detail.you: Small badge on the scoreboard row of the app user. Keep short, about 3 characters.
detail.player_fallback: Name shown on the scoreboard for a player whose name is unknown. {slot} = player number in the match, e.g. 4.
detail.item_unknown: Tooltip for an item slot with an unknown item. {id} = item ID number, e.g. 1234. Item is a Deadlock game term.

result.unscored: Result text in the match summary when the match has no win or loss.
result.team_won: Result text in the match summary. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Team names are Deadlock game terms.
result.unknown: Result text in the match summary when the winner is not known.

mode.ranked: Match mode label in the match summary. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
mode.unranked: Match mode label in the match summary. Deadlock game term, match the game's own translation.
mode.streetBrawl: Match mode label in the match summary. Street Brawl is a Deadlock game mode, match the game's own translation.
mode.custom: Match mode label in the match summary, for custom matches.
mode.bot: Match mode label in the match summary, for matches against bots.
mode.other: Match mode label in the match summary for modes that are not otherwise named.

col.items: Table column header on the scoreboard, the items a player ended with. Keep short, about 5 characters.
col.damage: Table column header on the scoreboard, damage dealt. Keep short, about 6 characters.

board.label: Screen reader label for the scoreboard table.
board.stat: Screen reader label for the first column header of the scoreboard, which holds stat names.
board.best: Screen reader and tooltip text marking a stat as the highest in the match.
board.unranked: Screen reader label for a player with no rank badge. Deadlock rank term.

detail.mvp: Small award badge on the scoreboard for the best player. Keep short, about 3 characters.
detail.key_player: Small award badge on the scoreboard for the key player of the losing team. Keep short, about 10 characters.
detail.avg_rank: Label next to a team's average rank badge on the scoreboard. Keep short, about 8 characters.

versus.above: Tooltip and screen reader text for a stat mark. The stat is higher than the user's own average on that hero. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
versus.below: Tooltip and screen reader text for a stat mark. The stat is lower than the user's own average on that hero. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
versus.equal: Tooltip and screen reader text for a stat mark. The stat is close to the user's own average on that hero.
versus.average: Small text under a stat. {value} = the user's average, e.g. "12". Keep short, about 8 characters.
versus.souls_rate: Small text under the souls stat. {value} = souls per minute average, e.g. "850". Souls is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 13 characters.
versus.hint: Tooltip on a stat comparison. {samples} = number of other matches on the same hero, e.g. 12. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
versus.summary: Summary line under the scoreboard. {samples} = number of other matches, e.g. 12. {better} = count of stats better, e.g. 3. {worse} = count of stats worse, e.g. 2.

export.group: Screen reader label for the group of buttons that export the scoreboard as an image.
export.save: Button on the match detail page that saves the scoreboard as an image file. Keep short, about 10 characters.
export.copy: Button on the match detail page that copies the scoreboard image to the clipboard. Keep short, about 10 characters.
export.working: Button text shown while the scoreboard image is being made. Keep short, about 15 characters.
export.saved: Toast message after the scoreboard image was saved to a file.
export.copied: Toast message after the scoreboard image was copied to the clipboard.
export.save_failed: Error toast when saving the scoreboard image failed. {error} = reason text, e.g. "Permission denied".
export.copy_failed: Error toast when copying the scoreboard image failed. {error} = reason text, e.g. "Clipboard unavailable".
export.made_with: Credit text in the footer of the exported scoreboard image. The app name follows it. Keep short, about 9 characters.
export.render_failed: Error toast when the scoreboard image could not be created.

replay.heading: Section heading on the match detail page for the minimap replay and timeline. Keep short, about 6 characters.
replay.map_aria: Screen reader label for the minimap showing player positions.
replay.no_paths: Notice under the replay section when position data is missing. The timeline shows deaths, objectives and item purchases.
replay.no_art: Small notice on the minimap when the map picture is missing. Positions are drawn on a plain background.
replay.no_events: Empty state in the replay timeline when the match has no events.
replay.no_kinds: Empty state in the replay timeline when all event type toggles are off.
replay.unknown: Fallback label for an unknown team in the replay tooltip. Keep short, about 7 characters.
replay.unknown_hero: Fallback label for an unknown hero in the replay tooltip. Hero is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 12 characters.
replay.dead: Status text in the minimap tooltip for a dead player. Keep short, about 4 characters.
replay.dot_dead: Screen reader label for a dead player's dot on the minimap. {label} = player and hero name, e.g. "Sam, Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
replay.camps: Toggle button above the replay map that shows or hides neutral jungle camps. Camp is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 5 characters.
replay.shop: Map tooltip title for the shop building on the replay map. Shop is a Deadlock game term and should match the game's own translation.
replay.teleporter: Map tooltip title for a teleporter on the replay map. Teleporter is a Deadlock game term and should match the game's own translation.
replay.camps_hint: Tooltip text for a neutral camp on the replay map, and for the Camps toggle button. Says camp timings are estimates.
replay.mid_boss_hint: Tooltip line for the Mid Boss on the replay map. Says respawn times are estimates. Mid Boss is a Deadlock game term.
replay.mid_boss_last_kill: Tooltip line for the Mid Boss on the replay map. {time} = match clock time, e.g. "12:34". Mid Boss is a Deadlock game term.
replay.object_destroyed_at: Tooltip line for a map objective (Guardian, Walker, etc.) in the replay map. {time} = match clock time, e.g. "12:34".
replay.object_damage: Small heading in a replay map objective tooltip, above a breakdown of damage by source (Gun, Spirit, Trooper).
replay.damage_gun: Label in a replay map objective tooltip for damage dealt by gun shots. Weapon damage is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 4 characters.
replay.damage_spirit: Label in a replay map objective tooltip for damage dealt by Spirit abilities. Spirit is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 6 characters.
replay.damage_trooper: Label in a replay map objective tooltip for damage dealt by troopers (lane minions). Trooper is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 8 characters.
replay.camp_weak: Replay map tooltip title for the lowest tier neutral camp. Camp is a Deadlock game term.
replay.camp_medium: Replay map tooltip title for the middle tier neutral camp. Camp is a Deadlock game term.
replay.camp_strong: Replay map tooltip title for the highest tier regular neutral camp. Camp is a Deadlock game term.
replay.camp_vault: Replay map tooltip title for the Vault, a special neutral camp. Vault is a Deadlock game term.
replay.play: Button label on the replay controls that starts playback. Keep short, about 4 characters.
replay.pause: Button label on the replay controls that pauses playback. Keep short, about 5 characters.
replay.speed: Option in the replay playback speed selector. {speed} = speed multiplier number, e.g. 2. Keep short, about 3 characters.
replay.speed_aria: Screen reader label for the playback speed selector in the replay controls.
replay.time: Replay time readout next to the scrubber. {current} = current match clock, e.g. "12:34". {total} = full match length, e.g. "38:10".
replay.scrubber_aria: Screen reader label for the time slider that scrubs through the match replay.
replay.kinds_aria: Screen reader label for the group of filter chips that choose which event types show on the replay timeline.
replay.kind_death: Filter chip on the replay timeline that toggles death events. Keep short, about 6 characters.
replay.kind_objective: Filter chip on the replay timeline that toggles objective events (Guardians, Walkers, etc.). Keep short, about 10 characters.
replay.kind_mid_boss: Filter chip on the replay timeline for Mid Boss events, also used as a label on the match front page. Mid Boss is a Deadlock game term.
replay.kind_item_buy: Filter chip on the replay timeline that toggles item purchase events. Keep short, about 9 characters.
replay.kind_item_sell: Filter chip on the replay timeline that toggles item sale events. Keep short, about 10 characters.
replay.kind_swing: Filter chip on the replay timeline that toggles big Soul lead changes between teams. Soul is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 16 characters.
replay.lane_death: Row label on the left of the replay timeline for the death events lane. Keep short, about 6 characters.
replay.lane_objective: Row label on the left of the replay timeline for the objective events lane. Keep short, about 10 characters.
replay.lane_mid_boss: Row label on the left of the replay timeline for the Mid Boss lane. Mid Boss is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 8 characters.
replay.lane_swing: Row label on the left of the replay timeline for the lane of big Soul lead changes. Keep short, about 6 characters.
replay.lane_item: Row label on the left of the replay timeline for the item buy and sell lane. Keep short, about 5 characters.
replay.marker_death: Screen reader and tooltip text for a death marker on the replay timeline. {victim} = player name, e.g. "Sam". {killer} = killer name or hero, e.g. "Haze". {time} = match clock, e.g. "12:34".
replay.marker_objective: Screen reader and tooltip text for an objective marker on the replay timeline. {objective} = objective name, e.g. "Walker". {team} = team name, e.g. "Sapphire". {time} = match clock, e.g. "12:34".
replay.marker_mid_boss: Screen reader and tooltip text for a Mid Boss marker on the replay timeline. {team} = team that claimed it, e.g. "Amber". {time} = match clock, e.g. "12:34". Mid Boss is a Deadlock game term.
replay.marker_item_buy: Screen reader and tooltip text for an item purchase marker on the replay timeline. {player} = player name, e.g. "Sam". {item} = item name, e.g. "Spirit Lifesteal". {time} = match clock, e.g. "12:34".
replay.marker_item_sell: Screen reader and tooltip text for an item sale marker on the replay timeline. {player} = player name, e.g. "Sam". {item} = item name, e.g. "Spirit Lifesteal". {time} = match clock, e.g. "12:34".
replay.marker_swing: Screen reader and tooltip text for a net worth swing marker on the replay timeline. {team} = team name, e.g. "Amber". {souls} = number of Souls, e.g. "2,500". {time} = match clock, e.g. "12:34". Souls is a Deadlock game term.
replay.death_map: Toggle button above the replay that opens the death map view, which shows where deaths happened. Keep short, about 9 characters.
replay.my_deaths: Option in the death map player selector for the user's own deaths. Keep short, about 10 characters.
replay.death_step: Position counter in the death stepper toolbar. {index} = current death number, e.g. 3. {total} = number of deaths, e.g. 8.
replay.step_prev: Tooltip and screen reader label of the icon button in the death stepper that jumps to the previous death.
replay.step_next: Tooltip and screen reader label of the icon button in the death stepper that jumps to the next death.
replay.step_show_all: Button in the death stepper that ends stepping and shows all deaths on the map again. Keep short, about 8 characters.
replay.stepper_aria: Screen reader label for the death stepper toolbar that moves through deaths one by one.
replay.killer_slot: Fallback name for a killer whose identity is unknown, shown in the death map details. {slot} = player slot number, e.g. 4.
replay.death_respawn: Detail line for a selected death on the death map. {seconds} = respawn wait in seconds, e.g. 24.
replay.death_position: Detail line for a selected death on the death map. {x} and {y} = map coordinates, e.g. 1200 and 340.
replay.death_marker: Screen reader label for a death marker on the death map. {victim} = player name, e.g. "Sam". {time} = match clock, e.g. "12:34".
replay.killed_by: Detail line for a selected death on the death map. {killer} = killer's player name and hero, e.g. "Sam · Haze".
replay.filter_player: Label above the player dropdown in the death map filters. Keep short, about 6 characters.
replay.all_players: Option in the death map player dropdown that shows deaths for every player. Keep short, about 11 characters.
replay.filter_role: Label above the selector that chooses whether the death map shows the chosen player as victim or killer.
replay.role_victim: Option in the death map role selector. Shows deaths where the chosen player died. Keep short, about 6 characters.
replay.role_killer: Option in the death map role selector. Shows deaths where the chosen player got the kill. Keep short, about 6 characters.
replay.range_from: Label above the start handle of the death map time range slider. {time} = match clock, e.g. "05:00".
replay.range_to: Label above the end handle of the death map time range slider. {time} = match clock, e.g. "20:00".
replay.death_count: Summary in the death stepper toolbar when not stepping. {count} = number of deaths, e.g. 5. Plural forms.
replay.step_start: Button in the death stepper that starts stepping through deaths one by one. Keep short, about 12 characters.
replay.no_deaths: Empty state text in the death stepper when the current filter has no deaths. Keep short, about 10 characters.
replay.death_map_player: Screen reader label for the player dropdown on the death map.

grade.label: Label in the grade tooltip, next to the numeric score and letter, on a player's row in the match scoreboard. Keep short, about 5 characters.
grade.place_ordinal: Ordinal place in the match, used inside the grade label. {place} = number, e.g. 2 gives "2nd". Plural forms by ordinal category. Adjust each form to your language.
grade.aria: Screen reader label for the grade chip on a player's scoreboard row. {letter} = grade letter, e.g. "B+". {score} = number, e.g. 78. {place} = ordinal place, e.g. "2nd".
grade.chip_aria: Screen reader label for a player's grade chip on the match page. {letter} = grade letter, e.g. A. {score} = score, e.g. 87. {place} = placement in the match, e.g. 2nd.
grade.leaver: Tooltip for a flag icon on the scoreboard. Warns that a player left early, which skews all grades in the match.
grade.unchecked: Tooltip for a flag icon on the scoreboard. Says leavers were not checked, so the grade uses the game's own match data.
grade.farm_bonus: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. A bonus score from the team's farming. Farm means collecting Souls from troopers and camps.

metric.early_damage: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Damage dealt to heroes in the early game.
metric.late_damage: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Damage dealt to heroes in the late game.
metric.early_assists: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Kill assists in the early game.
metric.late_assists: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Kill assists in the late game.
metric.prebase_objective: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Damage dealt to objectives such as Guardians and Walkers, before the base.
metric.base_objective: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Damage dealt to base objectives such as Base Guardians, Shrines and the Patron. Deadlock game terms.
metric.damage_absorbed: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Damage the player took in place of teammates.
metric.ally_healing: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Healing done to teammates.
metric.heal_prevented: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Enemy healing the player prevented.
metric.barriers: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Barrier (shield) amount the player gave to teammates.
metric.cs: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Last hits on troopers and camps (creep score).
metric.kills: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Hero kills. Keep short, about 5 characters.
metric.deaths: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Times the player died. Keep short, about 6 characters.
metric.cc: Row label in the grade tooltip, followed by a number. Crowd control, the time enemies were stunned or slowed. Keep short, about 2 characters.

missing.details: Section heading on the page for a match whose data is missing. Covers the scoreboard and match details.
missing.replay: Section heading on the page for a match whose data is missing. Covers the replay state.
missing.lead: Intro paragraph on the page for a match that has no scoreboard. The Deadlock API is a third party data service and stays untranslated.
missing.badge_missing: Badge next to the match details heading when details are missing. Keep short, about 7 characters.
missing.badge_recovering: Badge next to the match details heading while Deadlock+ is recovering the match. Keep short, about 10 characters.
missing.eta_seconds: Progress text while a match is recovering. {count} = seconds left, e.g. 15. Unit is seconds.
missing.eta_minutes: Progress text while a match is recovering. {count} = minutes left, e.g. 3. Unit is minutes.
missing.paused: Status text on the missing match page when match recovery is paused.
missing.recover: Button on the missing match page that starts recovering this one match. Keep short, about 18 characters.
missing.recover_time: Small note next to the Recover button. Says how long recovery takes.
missing.consent_note: Small note next to the Recover button when the user already agreed to recovery. Says only this match is recovered.
missing.open_in_game: Hint on the missing match page. Tells the user to open this match in the game's Match History. Deadlock and Deadlock+ stay untranslated.
missing.sharing_off: Hint on the missing match page. "Share my matches" is the name of a setting, keep it matching that setting's label. Deadlock and Deadlock+ stay untranslated.
missing.sharing_link: Link text on the missing match page that opens the Settings page for match sharing.
missing.replay_available: Badge in the replay section of the missing match page. Replay can be watched. Keep short, about 9 characters.
missing.replay_expired: Badge in the replay section of the missing match page. Replay is too old and was deleted. Keep short, about 7 characters.
missing.replay_none: Badge in the replay section of the missing match page. No replay exists for this match. Keep short, about 13 characters.
missing.replay_days_left: Note in the replay section of the missing match page. {count} = days left, e.g. 5. Plural forms.
missing.replay_expired_note: Note in the replay section of the missing match page, shown with the Expired badge. Says how long replays are kept.
missing.replay_none_note: Note in the replay section of the missing match page. The Deadlock API is a third party data service and stays untranslated.
missing.replay_recoverable: Badge in the replay section of the missing match page. Replay is not there yet but can be recovered. Keep short, about 17 characters.
missing.replay_recoverable_note: Note in the replay section of the missing match page. The Deadlock API is a third party data service and stays untranslated.
missing.replay_unrecoverable: Badge in the replay section of the missing match page. Replay can never be recovered. Keep short, about 13 characters.
missing.replay_unrecoverable_note: Note in the replay section of the missing match page, shown with the unrecoverable badge.
missing.badge_not_applicable: Small badge on a match page that cannot have a scoreboard because of its game mode. Keep short, about 14 characters.
missing.not_applicable: Explanation on a match page with no scoreboard. Only ranked, unranked and Street Brawl are recovered. These are Deadlock game mode names, match the game's translation. Deadlock+ stays untranslated.

replay_status.available: Badge on the match detail page. A replay can be watched. Keep short, about 16 characters.
replay_status.recovering: Badge on the match detail page with a spinner. The replay is being recovered. Keep short, about 17 characters.
replay_status.recoverable: Badge on the match detail page. No replay yet, but one can be recovered. Keep short, about 13 characters.
replay_status.unrecoverable: Badge on the match detail page. The replay can no longer be recovered. Keep short, about 25 characters.
replay_status.expired: Badge on the match detail page. The replay is too old and was deleted. Keep short, about 15 characters.
replay_status.none: Badge on the match detail page. No replay exists for this match. Keep short, about 9 characters.
replay_status.recover: Button next to the replay badge on the match detail page that starts recovering the replay. Keep short, about 14 characters.
replay_status.recover_note: Tooltip on the Recover replay button. Recovery uses part of a daily limit of 40 matches. Keep the number 40.
replay_status.consent_note: Tooltip on the Recover replay button when the user already agreed to recovery. Only this replay is recovered, background recovery stays off.

detail.load_error: Error message. Shown on the match detail page when the match could not be loaded.

ping.heading: Section heading on the match detail page above the ping chart. Ping is network latency in milliseconds.
ping.source: Short source label for ping data that came from pinging the game server over ICMP. ICMP stays untranslated.
ping.source_engine: Source label under the Ping heading. The data came from the game's own connection stats.
ping.source_icmp: Source label under the Ping heading. The data came from pinging the game server (ICMP). ICMP stays untranslated.
ping.partial: Note after the source label under the Ping heading. Data only covers part of the match, from when recording began.
ping.avg: Label above the average ping number in the ping section. Keep short, about 7 characters.
ping.worst: Label above the highest ping number in the ping section. Keep short, about 5 characters.
ping.samples: Label above the number of ping measurements in the ping section. Keep short, about 7 characters.
ping.loading: Loading state text in the ping section on the match detail page.
ping.empty: Empty state text in the ping section when no ping data was recorded for the match.
ping.chart_aria: Screen reader label for the ping line chart on the match detail page.
ping.hint: Small hint text under the ping chart. Says ping is sampled once per second while Deadlock+ ran. Deadlock+ stays untranslated.

coverage.label: Screen reader label for the coverage summary strip at the top of the match history list.
coverage.details: Label in the coverage strip above a number showing how many matches have full details. Keep short, about 12 characters.
coverage.replays: Label in the coverage strip above a number showing how many matches have replays. Keep short, about 21 characters.
coverage.details_aria: Screen reader label for the full details figure in the coverage strip. {full} = matches with details, e.g. 42. {total} = all matches, e.g. 50.
coverage.replays_aria: Screen reader label for the replays figure in the coverage strip. {replays} = matches with a replay, e.g. 18. {recent} = recent matches counted, e.g. 30.
coverage.recover: Button in the coverage strip that opens the recovery panel. {count} = number of missing matches, e.g. 12. Keep short, about 20 characters.
coverage.recovering: Progress text in the coverage strip while recovery runs. {done} = matches recovered, e.g. 5. {total} = matches to recover, e.g. 12.
coverage.paused: Progress text in the coverage strip while recovery is paused. {done} = matches recovered, e.g. 5. {total} = matches to recover, e.g. 12.

recovery.title: Dialog title of the match recovery panel opened from match history.
recovery.close: Screen reader label and tooltip of the close icon button in the recovery panel.
recovery.consent: Consent text in the recovery panel and on a missing match page. Explains what recovery does and that it uses the Steam login saved on this PC. Steam is a brand name.
recovery.missing: Small label after a big number in the recovery panel. Number of missing matches. Keep short, about 7 characters.
recovery.badge_paused: Status badge in the recovery panel. Recovery is paused by the user. Keep short, about 6 characters.
recovery.badge_game: Status badge in the recovery panel. Recovery waits because the game is running. Deadlock stays untranslated. Keep short, about 16 characters.
recovery.badge_limit: Status badge in the recovery panel. Recovery waits because Steam's daily request limit was hit. Steam is a brand name. Keep short, about 19 characters.
recovery.eta_left: Time estimate in the recovery panel and status bar. {time} = duration text, e.g. "5 min" or "1 h 20 min".
recovery.eta_total: Time estimate in the recovery panel before starting. {time} = duration text, e.g. "5 min" or "1 h 20 min".
recovery.duration_minutes: Duration in minutes. {count} = number of minutes, e.g. 15. Keep short, about 6 characters.
recovery.duration_hours: Duration in whole hours. {count} = number of hours, e.g. 2. Keep short, about 5 characters.
recovery.duration_hours_minutes: Duration in hours and minutes. {hours} = whole hours, e.g. 1. {minutes} = minutes, e.g. 20. Keep short, about 12 characters.
recovery.progress_label: Screen reader label for the recovery progress bar group in the recovery panel.
recovery.accounts: Small heading in the recovery panel above the list of Steam accounts and how many requests each used today. Steam is a brand name.
recovery.start: Primary button in the recovery panel that starts recovery. {count} = number of matches to recover, e.g. 12. Keep short, about 14 characters.
recovery.pause: Button in the recovery panel that pauses a running recovery. Keep short, about 5 characters.
recovery.resume: Button in the recovery panel that continues a paused recovery. Keep short, about 6 characters.
recovery.limit_note: Status note in the recovery panel when the daily limit was reached. Recovery restarts by itself the next day.
recovery.step_details: Step label in the recovery panel progress. This step fills in missing match details. Keep short, about 15 characters.
recovery.step_replays: Step label in the recovery panel progress. This step fetches replays of recent matches. Keep short, about 14 characters.
recovery.start_failed: Toast shown when starting the recovery of past matches failed.
recovery.pause_failed: Toast shown when pausing the recovery of past matches failed.
recovery.resume_failed: Toast shown when resuming the recovery of past matches failed.
recovery.cancel_failed: Toast shown when stopping the recovery of past matches failed.
recovery.match_failed: Toast shown when recovering a single match failed.
recovery.replay_failed: Toast shown when recovering a single match from its replay file failed.

row_state.missing: Small badge on a row in the match history list. The match has no scoreboard details. Keep short, about 10 characters.
row_state.recovering: Small badge on a row in the match history list. The match is being recovered. Keep short, about 10 characters.

viewer_line.headline: Newspaper headline for the app user's own match. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". {kills}, {deaths}, {assists} = counts, e.g. 8, 3, 12. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
viewer_line.deck: Newspaper sub headline under a headline. {net_worth} = souls total, e.g. "24.5k". Net worth is counted in souls, a Deadlock game term.
viewer_line.deck_graded: Newspaper sub headline. {net_worth} = souls total, e.g. "24.5k". {letter} = grade, e.g. "B+". {place} = rank number, e.g. 2. {total} = player count, e.g. 12.

comeback.headline: Newspaper headline for a team that won after trailing. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". {deficit} = souls behind, e.g. "8.2k". Team names are Deadlock game terms.
comeback.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {deficit} = souls behind, e.g. "8.2k". {time} = match clock, e.g. "24:10". {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Team names are Deadlock game terms.

critics_top.headline: Newspaper headline for the top graded player. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
critics_top.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {player} = player name, e.g. "Sam". {letter} = grade, e.g. "A". {total} = player count, e.g. 12. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated.

first_blood.headline: Newspaper headline for the first kill of the match. {hero} = hero name of the killer, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
first_blood.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {player} = killer name, e.g. "Sam". {victim_hero} = hero name of the victim, e.g. "Seven". {time} = match clock, e.g. "3:20". Hero is a Deadlock game term.

mid_boss.headline: Newspaper headline for the team that claimed the Mid Boss. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Mid Boss and team names are Deadlock game terms.
mid_boss.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". {time} = match clock, e.g. "20:15". "It" is the Mid Boss, a Deadlock game term.
mid_boss.deck_split: Newspaper sub headline when one team killed the Mid Boss and the other claimed it. {killer} and {team} = team names. {time} = match clock, e.g. "20:15". Mid Boss is a Deadlock game term.

guardian_fall.headline: Newspaper headline for the first Guardian destroyed. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Guardian and team names are Deadlock game terms.
guardian_fall.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {owner} = team name that lost it, e.g. "The Hidden King". {time} = match clock, e.g. "9:40". Guardian is a Deadlock game term.

walker_fall.headline: Newspaper headline for the first Walker destroyed. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Walker and team names are Deadlock game terms.
walker_fall.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {owner} = team name that lost it, e.g. "The Hidden King". {time} = match clock, e.g. "14:05". Walker is a Deadlock game term.

base_guardian_fall.headline: Newspaper headline for the first Base Guardian destroyed. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Base Guardian and team names are Deadlock game terms.
base_guardian_fall.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {owner} = team name that lost it, e.g. "The Hidden King". {time} = match clock, e.g. "22:30". Base Guardian is a Deadlock game term.

shrine_fall.headline: Newspaper headline for a Shrine destroyed. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Shrine and team names are Deadlock game terms.
shrine_fall.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {owner} = team name that lost it, e.g. "The Hidden King". {time} = match clock, e.g. "26:00". Shrine is a Deadlock game term.

patron_fall.headline: Newspaper headline for the Patron destroyed, ending the match. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". Patron and team names are Deadlock game terms.
patron_fall.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {owner} = team name that lost its Patron, e.g. "The Hidden King". {time} = match clock, e.g. "35:12". Patron is a Deadlock game term.

top_damage.headline: Newspaper headline for the player with the most damage. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
top_damage.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {player} = player name, e.g. "Sam". {damage} = player damage total, e.g. "32.4k".

top_healing.headline: Newspaper headline for the player with the most healing. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Dynamo". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
top_healing.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {player} = player name, e.g. "Sam". {healing} = healing total, e.g. "18.1k".

richest.headline: Newspaper headline for the player with the highest net worth. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". Hero is a Deadlock game term.
richest.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {player} = player name, e.g. "Sam". {net_worth} = souls total, e.g. "28.9k". Souls is a Deadlock game term.

most_last_hits.headline: Newspaper headline for the player with the most last hits. Plural forms. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". {count} = number of last hits, e.g. 240. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
most_last_hits.deck: Newspaper sub headline. {player} = player name, e.g. "Sam".

kit.weather: Small section heading on the front page newspaper for the connection quality box. Keep short, about 7 characters.
kit.box_score: Section heading and screen reader label on the front page newspaper for the table of teams and players.
kit.critics: Section heading on the front page newspaper for player grades. Plays on newspaper critics.
kit.lane_report: Section heading on the front page newspaper for lane results. Lane is a Deadlock game term.
kit.in_brief: Section heading on the front page newspaper for a list of short facts. Keep short, about 8 characters.
kit.objectives: Section heading on the front page newspaper for the objectives timeline. Objectives are Deadlock game terms.
kit.kills: Section heading and screen reader label on the front page newspaper for team kill totals.
kit.hero: Screen reader column header in the front page player table. Hero is a Deadlock game term.
kit.kda: Screen reader column header in the front page player table for kills/deaths/assists. Keep the slashes.
kit.net_worth: Screen reader column header in the front page player table for total souls. Souls is a Deadlock game term.
kit.grade: Screen reader column header in the front page player table for the letter grade.

front_page.open: Button on the match detail page that opens the newspaper style front page recap for the match. Keep short, about 10 characters.
front_page.open_match: Button on the post match front page (newspaper style recap). Opens the full match page. Keep short, about 15 characters.
front_page.close: Button that closes the front page dialog. Keep short, about 5 characters.
front_page.dialog: Screen reader label for the front page dialog. {id} = match ID number, e.g. 12345678.
front_page.loading: Loading message while the front page newspaper is being built.
front_page.name: Newspaper name at the top of the front page. "Dispatch" is the newspaper word. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated.
front_page.edition: Edition line in the newspaper masthead. {id} = match ID number, e.g. 12345678. "Extra!" is the newspaper cry.
front_page.kicker_viewer: Small tag above the main headline when the story is about the app user's own match. Keep short, about 10 characters.
front_page.photo_caption: Photo caption under the hero picture. {hero} = hero name, e.g. "Haze". {kills}, {deaths}, {assists} = counts, e.g. 8, 3, 12. Valve is a company name, keep it untranslated.
front_page.place_of: Rank in the player grades. {place} = rank, e.g. "2" or "2nd". {total} = player count, e.g. 12. Keep short, about 7 characters.
front_page.critics_grading: Status text in the critics box while player grades are being worked out. Keep short, about 10 characters.
front_page.critics_pending: Status text in the critics box when grades are not ready yet. Keep short, about 14 characters.

lane.lead: Lane report line. {team} = team name, e.g. "The Archmother". {amount} = souls lead, e.g. "1.2k". "10:00" is a match clock time. Team names are Deadlock game terms.
lane.even: Lane report line when the lane was tied at the 10 minute mark. "10:00" is a match clock time.
lane.matchup: Lane report line listing the two heroes. {hidden_king} = hero name on The Hidden King's side, e.g. "Haze". {archmother} = hero name on The Archmother's side. Hero is a Deadlock game term.

weather.forecast_clear: Weather forecast word in the front page connection box, for a good connection. Keep short, about 11 characters.
weather.forecast_fair: Weather forecast word in the front page connection box, for an okay connection. Keep short, about 4 characters.
weather.forecast_overcast: Weather forecast word in the front page connection box, for a poor connection. Keep short, about 8 characters.
weather.forecast_storm: Weather forecast word in the front page connection box, for a bad connection. Keep short, about 6 characters.
weather.ping: Line in the front page connection box. {avg} = average ping in milliseconds, e.g. 42. {worst} = worst ping in milliseconds, e.g. 120. Keep "ms".
weather.jitter: Line in the front page connection box. {jitter} = ping variation in milliseconds, e.g. 8. Keep "ms".

objective.short_guardian: Tiny marker letter on the front page objectives timeline for a Guardian. Deadlock game term. Keep short, 1 to 2 characters.
objective.short_walker: Tiny marker letter on the front page objectives timeline for a Walker. Deadlock game term. Keep short, 1 to 2 characters.
objective.short_base_guardian: Tiny marker on the front page objectives timeline for a Base Guardian. Deadlock game term. Keep short, 2 characters.
objective.short_shrine: Tiny marker letter on the front page objectives timeline for a Shrine. Deadlock game term. Keep short, 1 to 2 characters.
objective.short_patron: Tiny marker letter on the front page objectives timeline for a Patron. Deadlock game term. Keep short, 1 to 2 characters.
objective.short_core: Tiny marker letter on the front page objectives timeline for a Core. Deadlock game term. Keep short, 1 to 2 characters.
objective.short_mid_boss: Tiny marker on the front page objectives timeline for the Mid Boss. Deadlock game term. Keep short, 2 characters.
objective.short_unknown: Tiny marker letter on the front page objectives timeline for an unknown objective. Keep short, 1 to 2 characters.

export.group: Screen reader label for the group of buttons that export the front page as an image.
export.saved: Toast message after the front page image was saved to a file.
export.copied: Toast message after the front page image was copied to the clipboard.
export.render_failed: Error toast when the front page image could not be created.
